selection_rationale: Longitudinal original research on Paraguay's economic formation and history, monetary institutions, public and private banks and the Ueno bank resolution announced on 3 November 2026. The preexisting September country dossier does not address banking history and current prudential crisis at this depth.
contrary_evidence: Sovereign investment-grade ratings and satisfactory aggregate banking ratios do not establish that every individual bank has adequate capital, but Ueno failure alone does not establish system-wide insolvency.
Paraguay's 2026 growth projections and pre-crisis capital ratios are of distinct dates and should not be read as post-intervention indicators.
The Paraguayan state's 19th century industry and state intervention do not demonstrate that it was inevitably destined to industrialize without the Triple Alliance War.
Corruption or conflict-of-interest allegations surrounding political and banking figures are not criminal convictions or proof of specific wrongdoing.
Public deposits reportedly held at Ueno are exposures, not yet established final losses; recovery is unknown.
limitations: Cutoff is November 4, 2026; Ueno asset valuations, coverage, claims ranking, payouts and criminal proceedings continue to evolve.
Historical accounts of demographic loss during the Triple Alliance War differ; a single death toll is deliberately avoided.
The historical figures on bank failures and estimated costs depend on institutional definitions and the period measured.
The 2026 GDP and fiscal estimates are forecasts published before the resolution, not final year results.
Reported Ueno public-deposit exposure of US$800–850 million and IPS exposure around US$380 million require subsequent official reconciliation.
Historical country case and modern banking supervision are linked through documented mechanisms rather than direct uninterrupted causation.
